messages.body_plain:

You should be able to represent all your data in a single VCF file. I believe the `vcf-concat` program from the vcftools suite should be able to concatenate your vcf files for you.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] index of association
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I think a relevant question is why do you have your data organized into separate files? If you have *g.vcf files created by the GATK's haplotype caller than you should run their GenotypeGVCF (https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/3.8-0/org_broadinstitute_gatk_tools_walkers_variantutils_GenotypeGVCFs.php) on them to create one file. If this is not the case then I think you should consider recalling your variants in a manner that results in one file. The VCF file will only have information on the variable positions. So if a position was variable in one individual but not in another that second one will have no information for that position. If you call variants over all your samples at once the variant caller should provide information on invariant sites (homozygous for the reference allele) if the position is variable in one of the other samples.

Good luck!
Brian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Calculating Nei's genetic distance and pairwise Fst from HLA allele frequencies
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] Calculating Nei's genetic distance and pairwise Fst from HLA allele frequencies
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I believe you cannot calculate pairwise Fst with allele frequency data since you don't have any information on heterozygosity.

That being said, you might be able to simulate populations using the rgenotypes function from the mmod package and calculate the statistics on the simulated populations and get confidence intervals. That being said, the function can only simulation one locus and one population at a time, so you will have to construct a couple of loops/lapply functions to get the job done for each of your populations and loci.

Because this question is more general in scope and not specific to poppr, I would recommend posting any questions on the above procedure to the R-SIG-GENETICS mailing list: https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-sig-genetics

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] index of association
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

In general, a high p-value of the index of association will indicate that you failed to reject the null hypothesis of unlinked loci in your population based on this test of multilocus linkage.

That being said, the documentation for ia has several relevant resources. I would recommend reading Agapow and Burt, 2001; and Smith et al. 1993 for details and caveats. Additionally, you may want to peruse the fifth chapter of my dissertation, which explores the limitations of this index and contains more references: https://zkamvar.github.io/dissertation/5-factors-influencing-inference-of-clonality-in-diploid-populations.html

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: AMOVA on SNP data in CSV file
messages.subject_clean: AMOVA on SNP data in CSV file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Meki,

Your data are coded in the correct format for the genlight objects. You should read adegenet's "genomics" tutorial: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials. Moreover, because AMOVA requires population strata, you should read the "strata" tutorial in the page I just linked.

Before you start AMOVA, you should also read the AMOVA manual page for poppr: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/poppr.amova.html

To prepare your data specifically, you will need to do three steps:

1. read the data in with read.table
2. extract the genotype matrix without the metadata and transpose it
3. convert these data to a genlight object

library("poppr")

# Data path can be a path on your computer
data_path <- "https://groups.google.com/group/poppr/attach/3753c7045bd07/example%20data.csv?part=0.1&authuser=0"

# Extract first line containing pouplations, split it by comma, and then remove the first empty string
my_populations <- strsplit(readLines(data_path, 1L), ",")[[1]][-1]

# Read the data into a data frame
myData <- read.table(data_path, sep = ",", skip = 1L, header = TRUE)

# Create a new genlight by transposing the data, assigning the locus names and strata
myData.gl <- new("genlight", t(myData[, -1]),
                 loc.names = myData$ID,
                 strata = data.frame(population = my_populations))

# AMOVA
poppr.amova(myData.gl, ~population)

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject_clean: AMOVA on SNP file in .txt format
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm searching to perform AMOVA on my dataset. But I have an error message that I don't know how eliminate it.
I have 252 genotypes and more than 18000 polymorfic SNPs. To facilitate the calculation I took only the first 100 markers.
These are my command lines:

file <- read.table("trial.txt", header=T)

tfile <- t(file[,1:ncol(file)])   #transpose table
colnames(tfile) = tfile[1, ]   #markers labels
tfile = tfile[-1, ]

# to change rownames because the transposition don't leave the labels "ID"
g <- tfile
ID <- rownames(g)
rownames(g) <- NULL
fx <- cbind(ID,g)
View(fx)

x <- as.data.frame(fx, header=T) #trasform into a data.frame

locs <- x[, -c(1, 2)]
colnames(locs) <- gsub("\\-", "_", colnames(locs))

ind <- as.character(file$lines)     # labels of the individuals
population <- as.character(file$Pop)    # labels of the populations

id <- read.table("strata.txt", header=T)    # add strata

file_genind <- df2genind(locs, ploidy = 2, ind.names = ind, pop = population, strata = id, NA.char = "NA", type = "codom", sep = "") # conversion into a genind object

file_amova <- poppr.amova(file_genind, ~rep/year/plot)
Found 238 missing values.

3 loci contained missing values greater than 5%

Removing 3 loci: JHI_Hv50k_2016_206330, JHI_Hv50k_2016_206596, JHI_Hv50k_2016_20687
Error in if (any (as.numeric (unlist (x @all.names, use.names = FALSE)) ==:
   Missing value where TRUE / FALSE is needed
Additionally: Warning message:
In get_local_ploidy (x): NAs generated by transformation

Someone is able to help me, please?
Thanks,

Antonia

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

This is a bug in poppr. Thank you for providing a reproducible example. I've created an issue that you can use to track the status of the bug here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/190. It should be fixed within the hour and you can install the new version from github if you have a C compiler.

That being said, since you have 18K markers that appear to be bi-allelic, you may want to consider using the "genlight" object to store your data for this analysis. Details about that object type can be found in the "genomics" tutorial from adegenet: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials

Hope that helps,
Zhian

I am working with AFLP data and am running some post hoc tests using poppr and specifically looking at population structure using NJ trees. I have been unable to find other people with this issue and feel that it might be something simple I have overlooked.

Error in dimnames(x) <- dn :
  length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent

Thank you for your time and advice,

Elliot Weidow
